title: Move Negative Numbers to Front
statement: Given an integer array nums, move all negative numbers to the front. Relative order does not have to be preserved.
mnemonic: Find wrong left + wrong right + swap
think: What is the task asking? Given an integer array nums, move all negative numbers to the front. Relative order does not have to be preserved.
What is the key operation? Identify the repeated action over the input.
What wording signals stand out? partition array, move negatives, two pointers.
What is the brute force idea? Use extra loops or repeated checks.
What is the better/optimal idea? Use a clean two pointers solution.
What are the edge cases? Empty-like input, single values, duplicates, and boundaries.
What is the complexity? For most of these easy tasks, aim for O(n) time unless sorting is required.
How would I explain it in an interview? State the pattern, the key operation, and the complexity.
interview: I would solve it using Two Pointers. I would first identify the core operation, then apply a simple two pointers approach and mention the complexity.
